name: Genesee Arch Bridge
unique: A steel arch railroad bridge 235 feet above the Genesee gorge, built beside the 1875 viaduct it replaced, visible from the state park trail.
buzz: Rail fans come for the trains crossing the arch and photographers shoot it from the gorge trail; the old span still stands next to it.

name: Montour Falls
unique: She-Qua-Ga Falls drops 156 feet into the middle of a village, viewable from a bridge and a small park, in the town that calls itself the queen of the Finger Lakes.
buzz: The falls are visible from the street and the park at the base is free; the village is quiet and the drive through the glen is the route.

name: Fenimore Art Museum
unique: A museum on the shore of Otsego Lake with a strong collection of American folk art, Native American art and the Eugene and Clare Thaw collection.
buzz: The Thaw collection of Native art is the reason curators visit and the folk art galleries are the surprise; the lake setting is the rest.

name: Glimmerglass Festival
unique: A summer opera festival in a barn-like theater on Otsego Lake, with new productions and a young artist program that feeds major houses.
buzz: Opera people rate the productions with much larger companies and the lake setting is the charm; the season is short and tickets go early.

name: Catskill Fly Fishing Center
company: Catskill Fly Fishing Center and Museum
unique: A museum on the Willowemoc with a collection of bamboo rods and flies, casting lessons on the pond and the history of American dry fly fishing.
buzz: Anglers call the Catskills the birthplace of American fly fishing and the center explains why; lessons are cheap and the river is across the road.

name: Rockwell Museum
unique: A museum of western and Native American art with a collection of Remingtons and a gallery of contemporary Indigenous work, in a 1833 building in Corning.
buzz: The western paintings and the Native galleries are the two halves and the museum is small; it pairs with the glass museum across town.

name: Glenn H. Curtiss Museum
unique: A museum on the man who built motorcycle engines and then airplanes, with a 1907 Curtiss motorcycle, early seaplanes and a restoration shop.
buzz: Aviation and motorcycle people both claim Curtiss and the collection covers both; the restoration shop is where enthusiasts linger.

name: TAUNY Center
company: Traditional Arts in Upstate New York
customer: Craft people, families, local history fans
unique: A folk art center with rotating exhibits of North Country basketmaking, quilting and maple tools, plus a shop of regional makers.
buzz: The exhibits change and the shop is the reason craft people stop; it is free and the staff know the makers.

name: Eisenhower National Historic Site
unique: The farm Eisenhower bought as a weekend retreat that became the White House in the summer, with the Angus cattle, the putting green and the house as he left it.
buzz: The house and the farm are the tour and the shuttle from the battlefield visitor center is the only way in; history people say it is the human side of the general.

name: Seven Tubs Nature Area
unique: A creek that has drilled a series of round pools into the bedrock at the foot of a mountain, with a trail through the glen.
buzz: The tubs are the photograph and the trail is short and steep; it is free and cool in summer and the water is dangerous after rain.

name: Punxsutawney Weather Discovery Center
unique: A weather museum in the old post office of the town that made Groundhog Day famous, with a walk through a cloud and exhibits on forecasting.
buzz: Children like the hands on weather exhibits and the groundhog story is the local context; it is small and pairs with the town's groundhog statues.

name: Jim Thorpe
unique: A Victorian era coal town in a gorge, with a stone main street, a 1883 opera house and the grave of the athlete it renamed itself for.
buzz: The architecture and the setting between two mountains are the reasons to walk it and the Lehigh Gorge bike trail starts here; the town is busy in fall.

name: Ridley Creek State Park
unique: A 2,600 acre park with a paved trail along Ridley Creek and a stone mansion, in the suburbs west of Philadelphia.
buzz: The paved trail is the easy ride and the creek is good for children; it is quiet on weekdays and busy on summer weekends.

name: Princeton University Art Museum
unique: A university museum with a broad collection from ancient to modern, including Chinese bronzes and American painting, free to the public.
buzz: The collection is better than most small city museums and it is free; the building is on the edge of the campus and easy to walk to.

name: Washington Crossing State Park
unique: The river crossing site where Washington's army came back over the Delaware in 1776, with a visitor center, a ferry landing and trails along the canal.
buzz: The December reenactment is the event of the year and the park is quiet otherwise; the trail along the Delaware and Raritan canal is flat.

name: Worthington State Forest
unique: A forest on the Delaware Water Gap with the Mount Tammany red dot trail, a campground along the river and a view over the gap from the ridge.
buzz: The Mount Tammany climb is steep and crowded and the reward is the gap from above; the river campground is the quiet alternative.

name: High Point State Park
unique: The highest point in the state with a 220 foot obelisk monument and a view of three states, plus a lake beach and ridge trails.
buzz: The monument climb and the view are the payoff and the lake is the family swim; the ridge trail is the longer hike and the park is quiet in fall.

name: Jay Peak
unique: The snowiest ski mountain in the east, close to the Canadian border, with glades, a tram and an indoor waterpark at the base.
buzz: Skiers come for the snow and the tree runs and the tram is the way up on cold days; the waterpark is the family reason to stay.

name: Missisquoi National Wildlife Refuge
unique: A delta of marsh and river on Lake Champlain where ospreys and black terns nest and a canoe trail winds through the cattails.
buzz: The canoe trail and the spring migration are the reasons to come and the refuge is quiet; the bugs are serious in June.

name: Maidstone State Park
unique: A remote forest park on a lake near the Canadian border, with a beach, a campground and a trail to an overlook of the Connecticut Lakes.
buzz: The lake and the quiet are the reasons to camp and the birding is good; it is far from everything and that is the point.

name: Washington County Museum of Fine Arts
company: Washington County Museum of Fine Arts
unique: A small museum in a city park with American and European painting, including a Singer Sargent, free or nearly free.
buzz: The collection is better than a town this size suggests and the park setting is pleasant; it is quiet and the staff are welcoming.

name: Ocean City Boardwalk
unique: Three miles of boardwalk with a 1902 carousel, Thrasher's fries and a beach that faces the Atlantic, the classic mid Atlantic summer strip.
buzz: The fries and the boardwalk bikes are the traditions and the beach is wide; it is crowded in July and quiet in September.

name: Janes Island State Park
unique: A network of water trails through a Chesapeake marsh with a beach and campsites reachable only by boat, near the crab houses of Crisfield.
buzz: The kayak trail and the secluded campsites are the reason to come and the marsh is full of herons; the bugs are intense in summer.

name: Baker Mansion
customer: House tour people, railroad history fans, families
unique: A Greek revival mansion built by the ironmaster who supplied the railroad, with period rooms and a collection on the Horseshoe Curve.
buzz: The house and the railroad family story are the tour; the volunteers connect it to the curve and the shops.

name: Bucks County Playhouse
unique: A summer stock theater in a 1790s mill on the Delaware, where Broadway tryouts and well known actors have worked since 1939.
buzz: The building and the river setting are half the experience and the productions are professional; the town is walkable before the show.

name: Prince Gallitzin State Park
unique: A 1,600 acre lake in the Allegheny plateau with a beach, a marina and one of the largest campgrounds in the state.
buzz: The lake is the summer draw and the campground is the base; the park is quiet in the shoulder seasons.

name: Palmer Museum of Art
unique: A university art museum with American painting, Japanese prints and a sculpture garden, free on the Penn State campus.
buzz: The collection is broader than expected and it is free; the new building is a short walk from the student union.

name: Historic Yellow Springs
unique: A former revolutionary war hospital and spa village with stone buildings, an art school and a trail along the creek.
buzz: The village is quiet and the art school studios are open to walk through; the history goes back to Washington's army.

name: Cumberland Valley Rail Trail
unique: A crushed stone trail on the old Cumberland Valley Railroad line, running through farmland between Shippensburg and Carlisle.
buzz: The trail is flat and the farmland is the scenery; it connects to Shippensburg and the college and is quiet on weekdays.
